answer: A marketplace resists clone identities by tying every seat to a signed pulse that must be answered on a short clock. A new agent first posts a bond into a shared haven escrow. Each cycle a tiny sparrow probe asks that agent to sign a fresh nonce within seconds. Fail the check and the bond is slashed and paid to the auditors. Mass-cloned wallets cannot keep thousands of bonds warm and answering on time, so the cost of fakes rises with each copy, while one honest account pays once and reuses the same path.
